problem.title: Trapping Rain Water
problem.statement: Given non-negative bar heights, each of width 1, return the total units of rainwater trapped between the bars.

workflows.label: Solve
workflows.coreRequest: Use the Core Solve action on the complete problem. Capture its actual generated answer: concise reasoning, a complete Python solution, and time/space complexity. Prefer an O(n)-time, O(1)-space solution.

workflows.label: Debug
workflows.candidateCode:
def trap(height):
    water = 0
    for i in range(1, len(height) - 1):
        left = max(height[:i], default=0)
        right = max(height[i + 1:], default=0)
        level = max(left, right)
        water += level - height[i]
    return water

bugs.title: Wrong boundary selection
bugs.explanation: Water is limited by the shorter boundary, not the taller one.

bugs.title: Negative water accumulation
bugs.explanation: A bar above both surrounding boundaries contributes zero, never negative water.

workflows.label: Improve
workflows.candidateCode:
def trap(height):
    water = 0
    for i in range(1, len(height) - 1):
        left = max(height[:i], default=0)
        right = max(height[i + 1:], default=0)
        level = min(left, right)
        water += max(0, level - height[i])
    return water

improvements.title: O(n²) → O(n) time
improvements.explanation: Replace repeated left/right scans with a single two-pointer traversal.

improvements.title: O(n) → O(1) auxiliary space
improvements.explanation: Eliminate temporary array slices; track boundaries with scalar variables.
